strategies.summary: The current specialized CUDA path is almost certainly underutilizing the GPU: very low active warps (8.33%) and moderate SM throughput with low DRAM pressure indicate a latency/occupancy-limited direct kernel. Recast the custom transposed-convolution fast path around tiles that reuse the same input patch across multiple output channels so each loaded input value contributes to several accumulators before eviction.
implementation_hints: Keep the existing narrow guard in the forward path, but only dispatch the custom kernel for the exact benchmark-dominant case already identified in phase 1.
In `cuda_cu`, move from one-thread-per-output-element scalar accumulation to a block shape where threads collaborate on a small spatial tile and compute several output channels per tile.
Stage a local input patch and/or a strip of weights in shared memory or read-only cache so the same `x[n, ic, iy, ix]` value is reused across multiple `oc` accumulations.
Prefer fewer live accumulators per thread than a fully unrolled scalar kernel; the NCU evidence shows register pressure is already a likely limiter in this workload class.
Preserve the C++ binding shape contract in `cuda_cpp`; only expose one benchmark-specialized entrypoint and retain PyTorch fallback in `forward_stmt_2`.

risk_notes: Shared-memory tiling can easily overgrow register/shared usage and further hurt occupancy.
Transposed-convolution indexing is easy to get wrong at padding boundaries.
A narrow win may vanish if the cuDNN root already exploits Tensor Core-friendly NHWC scheduling better than the custom kernel.

constant/read-only caching for the small 3x7 kernel footprint

review_notes.openai-compatible: Strong primary direction for a custom kernel: output-channel tiling and input reuse fit the likely bottleneck profile better than scalar mapping. Good upside, but indexing complexity and occupancy/reg-pressure tradeoffs make execution risk nontrivial.
review_notes.claude-compatible: Directly targets the root cause: very low active warp utilization and poor input reuse. Output-channel tiling with shared-memory staging is the canonical fix for this occupancy/latency-bound profile. Expected gain range (1.15x-1.5x) is plausible and risk is manageable if tiling parameters are tuned conservatively. Overlap with strategy_02 means these two should be evaluated together to avoid redundant effort.
review_notes.gemini-compatible: Excellent strategy. Tiling across output channels and reusing input patches via shared memory is the standard and most effective way to optimize direct convolutions, directly addressing the low arithmetic intensity and occupancy issues.

Register tiling to hold2x2 or 4x1 accumulators is a lower-complexity entry point and a good starting candidate before committing to full shared-memory tiling. Slightly lower ceiling than strategy_01 but also slightly lower implementation risk.
